verses.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־ לֵוִֽי׃ בַּת־
verses.transliteration: way·yê·leḵ ’îš mib·bêṯ lê·wî way·yiq·qaḥ ’eṯ- lê·wî baṯ-
verses.literal: - Now a man of the house of Levi married - a Levite woman

verses.original: הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתַּ֥הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי־ ה֔וּא ט֣וֹב וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: hā·’iš·šāh wat·ta·har wat·tê·leḏ bên wat·tê·re ’ō·ṯōw kî- hū ṭō·wḇ wat·tiṣ·pə·nê·hū šə·lō·šāh yə·rā·ḥîm
verses.literal: and she conceived and gave birth to a son When she saw - that he [was a] beautiful [child] she hid him for three months

verses.original: יָכְלָ֣ה וְלֹא־ עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח־ לוֹ֙ גֹּ֔מֶא תֵּ֣בַת וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם הַיֶּ֔לֶד בָּהּ֙ אֶת־ וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל־ שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃
verses.transliteration: yā·ḵə·lāh wə·lō- ‘ō·wḏ haṣ·ṣə·p̄î·nōw wat·tiq·qaḥ- lōw gō·me tê·ḇaṯ wat·taḥ·mə·rāh ḇa·ḥê·mār ū·ḇaz·zā·p̄eṯ wat·tā·śem hay·ye·leḏ bāh ’eṯ- wat·tā·śem bas·sūp̄ ‘al- śə·p̄aṯ hay·’ōr
verses.literal: But when she could no longer hide him she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch Then she placed the child in [the basket] and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile

verses.original: אֲחֹת֖וֹ וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה־ יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: ’ă·ḥō·ṯōw wat·tê·ṯaṣ·ṣaḇ mê·rā·ḥōq lə·ḏê·‘āh mah- yê·‘ā·śeh lōw
verses.literal: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him

verses.original: בַּת־ פַּרְעֹה֙ וַתֵּ֤רֶד לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל־ הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל־ יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת־ הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת־ אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ
verses.transliteration: baṯ- par·‘ōh wat·tê·reḏ lir·ḥōṣ ‘al- hay·’ōr wə·na·‘ă·rō·ṯe·hā hō·lə·ḵōṯ ‘al- yaḏ hay·’ōr wat·tê·re ’eṯ- hat·tê·ḇāh bə·ṯō·wḵ has·sūp̄ wat·tiš·laḥ ’eṯ- ’ă·mā·ṯāh wat·tiq·qå̄·ḥɛ·hå̄
verses.literal: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile and her attendants were walking along the riverbank . . . And when she saw - the basket among the reeds she sent - her maidservant to retrieve it

verses.original: וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת־ הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה־ נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר זֶֽה׃ הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים מִיַּלְדֵ֥י
verses.transliteration: wat·tip̄·taḥ wat·tir·’ê·hū ’eṯ- hay·ye·leḏ wə·hin·nêh- na·‘ar bō·ḵeh wat·taḥ·mōl ‘ā·lāw wat·tō·mer zeh hā·‘iḇ·rîm mî·yal·ḏê
verses.literal: When she opened it she saw - the child and behold the little boy was crying So she had compassion on him and said This is one of the Hebrew children

verses.original: אֲחֹתוֹ֮ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה֒ בַּת־ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת וְתֵינִ֥ק הַיָּֽלֶד׃ לָ֖ךְ אֶת־
verses.transliteration: ’ă·ḥō·ṯōw wat·tō·mer ’el- par·‘ōh baṯ- ha·’ê·lêḵ wə·qā·rā·ṯî lāḵ min hā·‘iḇ·rî·yōṯ ’iš·šāh mê·ne·qeṯ wə·ṯê·niq hay·yā·leḏ lāḵ ’eṯ-
verses.literal: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you -

verses.original: לֵ֑כִי פַּרְעֹ֖ה בַּת־ וַתֹּֽאמֶר־ לָ֥הּ הָֽעַלְמָ֔ה וַתֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַתִּקְרָ֖א אֶת־ הַיָּֽלֶד׃ אֵ֥ם
verses.transliteration: lê·ḵî par·‘ōh baṯ- wat·tō·mer- lāh hā·‘al·māh wat·tê·leḵ wat·tiq·rā ’eṯ- hay·yā·leḏ ’êm
verses.literal: Go ahead Pharaoh’s daughter told her And the girl went and called - the boy’s mother

verses.original: פַּרְעֹ֗ה בַּת־ וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת־ הַזֶּה֙ הַיֶּ֤לֶד וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת־ שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ הָאִשָּׁ֛ה וַתִּקַּ֧ח הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: par·‘ōh baṯ- wat·tō·mer lāh hê·lî·ḵî ’eṯ- haz·zeh hay·ye·leḏ wə·hê·ni·qi·hū lî wa·’ă·nî ’et·tên ’eṯ- śə·ḵā·rêḵ hā·’iš·šāh wat·tiq·qaḥ hay·ye·leḏ wat·tə·nî·qê·hū
verses.literal: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her Take - this child and nurse him for me and I will pay - your wages So the woman took the boy and nursed him

verses.original: הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיִגְדַּ֣ל וַתְּבִאֵ֙הוּ֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְבַת־ וַֽיְהִי־ לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ׃ מִן־ הַמַּ֖יִם
verses.transliteration: hay·ye·leḏ wa·yiḡ·dal wat·tə·ḇi·’ê·hū par·‘ōh lə·ḇaṯ- way·hî- lāh lə·ḇên wat·tiq·rā šə·mōw mō·šeh wat·tō·mer kî mə·šî·ṯi·hū min- ham·ma·yim
verses.literal: When the child had grown older she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter and he became her son She named him . . . Moses and explained . . . I drew him out of the water

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל־ אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ־ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bay·yā·mîm hā·hêm mō·šeh way·yiḡ·dal way·yê·ṣê ’el- ’e·ḥāw way·yar bə·siḇ·lō·ṯām way·yar ’îš miṣ·rî mak·keh ’îš- ‘iḇ·rî mê·’e·ḥāw
verses.literal: - One day . . . after Moses had grown up he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor He saw . . . an Egyptian beating . . . a Hebrew one of his own people

verses.original: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־ הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yi·p̄en kōh wā·ḵōh way·yar kî ’ên ’îš way·yaḵ ’eṯ- ham·miṣ·rî way·yiṭ·mə·nê·hū ba·ḥō·wl
verses.literal: After looking this way [and] that and seeing . . . no one he struck down - the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand

verses.original: הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בַּיּ֣וֹם וַיֵּצֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי־ אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: haš·šê·nî bay·yō·wm way·yê·ṣê wə·hin·nêh šə·nê- ’ă·nā·šîm ‘iḇ·rîm niṣ·ṣîm way·yō·mer lā·rā·šā‘ lām·māh ṯak·keh rê·‘e·ḵā
verses.literal: The next day [Moses] went out and saw two . . . Hebrews fighting He asked the one in the wrong Why are you attacking your companion

verses.original: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר הַלְהָרְגֵ֙נִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת־ הַמִּצְרִ֑י מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיִּירָ֤א וַיֹּאמַ֔ר הַדָּבָֽר׃ אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer mî śā·mə·ḵā lə·’îš śar wə·šō·p̄êṭ ‘ā·lê·nū ’at·tāh ’ō·mêr hal·hā·rə·ḡê·nî ka·’ă·šer hā·raḡ·tā ’eṯ- ham·miṣ·rî mō·šeh way·yî·rā way·yō·mar had·dā·ḇār ’ā·ḵên nō·w·ḏa‘
verses.literal: But the man replied Who made you ruler and judge over us Are you planning to kill me as you killed - the Egyptian Then Moses was afraid and thought This thing I have done has surely become known

verses.original: פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל־ הַבְּאֵֽר׃
verses.transliteration: par·‘ōh ’eṯ- had·dā·ḇār way·yiš·ma‘ haz·zeh way·ḇaq·qêš la·hă·rōḡ ’eṯ- mō·šeh mō·šeh way·yiḇ·raḥ mip·pə·nê p̄ar·‘ōh way·yê·šeḇ bə·’e·reṣ- miḏ·yān way·yê·šeḇ ‘al- hab·bə·’êr
verses.literal: When Pharaoh - - heard about this matter he sought to kill - Moses But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian where he sat down beside a well

verses.original: וּלְכֹהֵ֥ן מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֣בַע בָּנ֑וֹת וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה וַתִּדְלֶ֗נָה וַתְּמַלֶּ֙אנָה֙ אֶת־ הָ֣רְהָטִ֔ים לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת אֲבִיהֶֽן׃ צֹ֥אן
verses.transliteration: ū·lə·ḵō·hên miḏ·yān še·ḇa‘ bā·nō·wṯ wat·tā·ḇō·nāh wat·tiḏ·le·nāh wat·tə·mal·le·nāh ’eṯ- hā·rə·hā·ṭîm lə·haš·qō·wṯ ’ă·ḇî·hen ṣōn
verses.literal: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters and they came to draw water and fill - the troughs to water their father’s flock

verses.original: הָרֹעִ֖ים וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ וַיְגָרְשׁ֑וּם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיָּ֤קָם וַיּ֣וֹשִׁעָ֔ן וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־ צֹאנָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: hā·rō·‘îm way·yā·ḇō·’ū way·ḡā·rə·šūm mō·šeh way·yā·qām way·yō·wō·ši·‘ān way·yašq ’eṯ- ṣō·nām
verses.literal: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away Moses rose up to help them and watered - their flock

verses.original: וַתָּבֹ֕אנָה אֶל־ אֲבִיהֶ֑ן רְעוּאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַדּ֛וּעַ בֹּ֖א מִהַרְתֶּ֥ן הַיּֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tā·ḇō·nāh ’el- ’ă·ḇî·hen rə·‘ū·’êl way·yō·mer mad·dū·a‘ bō mi·har·ten hay·yō·wm
verses.literal: When [the daughters] returned to their father Reuel he asked them Why have you returned so early today

verses.original: מִצְרִ֔י הִצִּילָ֖נוּ מִיַּ֣ד הָרֹעִ֑ים וַתֹּאמַ֕רְןָ אִ֣ישׁ וְגַם־ דָּלֹ֤ה דָלָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־ הַצֹּֽאן׃
verses.transliteration: miṣ·rî hiṣ·ṣî·lā·nū mî·yaḏ hā·rō·‘îm wat·tō·mar·nā ’îš wə·ḡam- dā·lōh ḏā·lāh lā·nū way·yašq ’eṯ- haṣ·ṣōn
verses.literal: An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds they replied . . . He even drew water . . . for us and watered - the flock

verses.original: וְאַיּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־ בְּנֹתָ֖יו לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ן אֶת־ קִרְאֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ וְיֹ֥אכַל לָֽחֶם׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’ay·yōw way·yō·mer ’el- bə·nō·ṯāw lām·māh zeh hā·’îš ‘ă·zaḇ·ten ’eṯ- qir·’en lōw wə·yō·ḵal lā·ḥem
verses.literal: So where is he [their father] asked . . . . . . Why . . . did you leave the man behind - Invite him to have something to eat . . .

verses.original: מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיּ֥וֹאֶל לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אֶת־ הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיִּתֵּ֛ן אֶת־ בִתּ֖וֹ צִפֹּרָ֥ה לְמֹשֶֽׁה׃
verses.transliteration: mō·šeh way·yō·w·’el lā·še·ḇeṯ ’eṯ- hā·’îš way·yit·tên ’eṯ- ḇit·tōw ṣip·pō·rāh lə·mō·šeh
verses.literal: Moses agreed to stay with the man and he gave - his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage

verses.original: וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ גֵּרְשֹׁ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר הָיִ֔יתִי גֵּ֣ר נָכְרִיָּֽה׃פ בְּאֶ֖רֶץ
verses.transliteration: wat·tê·leḏ bên way·yiq·rā ’eṯ- šə·mōw gê·rə·šōm kî ’ā·mar hā·yî·ṯî gêr nā·ḵə·rî·yāh bə·’e·reṣ
verses.literal: And she gave birth to a son and [Moses] named him . . . . . . Gershom - saying I have become a foreigner in a foreign land

verses.original: וַיְהִי֩ הָֽרַבִּ֜ים הָהֵ֗ם בַיָּמִ֨ים מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיָּ֙מָת֙ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וַיֵּאָנְח֧וּ וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ מִן־ הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה שַׁוְעָתָ֛ם מִן־ הָעֲבֹדָֽה׃ וַתַּ֧עַל אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים
verses.transliteration: way·hî hā·rab·bîm hā·hêm ḇay·yā·mîm me·leḵ miṣ·ra·yim way·yā·māṯ ḇə·nê- yiś·rā·’êl way·yê·’ā·nə·ḥū way·yiz·‘ā·qū min- hā·‘ă·ḇō·ḏāh šaw·‘ā·ṯām min- hā·‘ă·ḇō·ḏāh wat·ta·‘al ’el- hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm
verses.literal: - After a long . . . time the king of Egypt died The Israelites . . . groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God

verses.original: אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע נַאֲקָתָ֑ם אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר בְּרִית֔וֹ אֶת־ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־ יִצְחָ֥ק וְאֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
verses.transliteration: ’ĕ·lō·hîm ’eṯ- way·yiš·ma‘ na·’ă·qā·ṯām ’ĕ·lō·hîm ’eṯ- way·yiz·kōr bə·rî·ṯōw ’eṯ- ’aḇ·rā·hām ’eṯ- yiṣ·ḥāq wə·’eṯ- ya·‘ă·qōḇ
verses.literal: So God - heard their groaning and He - remembered His covenant with Abraham . . . Isaac . . . and Jacob

verses.original: אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ וַיַּ֥רְא בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֱלֹהִֽים׃ס וַיֵּ֖דַע
verses.transliteration: ’ĕ·lō·hîm ’eṯ- way·yar bə·nê yiś·rā·’êl ’ĕ·lō·hîm way·yê·ḏa‘
verses.literal: God - saw the Israelites . . . and took notice
